key_insight: AlgoRAG shows that a domain-tuned retrieval-augmented generation system can deliver correct, pedagogically useful explanations for theoretical computer science topics that are difficult to teach with generic tools.
engineering_relevance: The paper demonstrates how curated retrieval, notation-aware matching, and pedagogical reranking can make LLMs more reliable for STEM education and proof-heavy reasoning tasks.
method: Built a TCS-specific RAG knowledge base from textbooks, slides, practice problems, proof templates, and worksheets.
Added mathematical entity recognition, notation-aware retrieval, and pedagogical reranking to improve answer quality.
Evaluated on 179 exam-style questions across analysis, recurrences, dynamic programming, graphs, NP-completeness, sorting, and divide-and-conquer.
evidence_signal: AlgoRAG achieved a 100% success rate on 179 curated questions with mean response time of 38.0 seconds, while pedagogical quality reached 0.7620 despite BLEU-4 being zero.
watch_item: Zero BLEU-4 shows that surface-form metrics can miss correct mathematical reasoning, so implementation should rely on domain-aware evaluation rather than n-gram scores alone.
paper_title: AlgoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Theoretical Computer Science Education -- A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for Algorithm Analysis and Complexity Theory
